problems.title: Check both roots after squaring two radical equations
problems.question: Solve (a) $\sqrt{x+5}=x-7$; (b) $\sqrt{x+15}=x+3$.
problems.idea: Each right side must be nonnegative before squaring.
steps: (a) Require x≥7. Squaring gives x+5=(x-7)², or (x-11)(x-4)=0. Only x=11 meets x≥7 and checks in the original equation.
(b) Require x≥-3. Squaring gives x+15=(x+3)², or (x+6)(x-1)=0. Only x=1 meets the condition and checks.

problems.title: A radical substitution clears a denominator
problems.question: Solve $3\sqrt{2x-1}-\sqrt{8x+17}=2(x-3)/\sqrt{2x-1}$.
steps: The equation becomes 3t-√(4t²+21)=t-5/t.
Rearrange to √(4t²+21)=2t+5/t. Both sides are positive.
Squaring gives 4t²+21=4t²+20+25/t², hence t²=25.

problems.title: Squaring a sum of two radicals
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt{x-6}+\sqrt{x-1}=\sqrt{x+15}$.
problems.idea: Use x≥6 and track the sign after the first squaring.
steps: Squaring gives 2√((x-6)(x-1))=22-x, so also x≤22.
Square again: 4(x²-7x+6)=(22-x)², giving 3x²+16x-460=0.
This factors as (x-10)(3x+46)=0. Only x=10 is in [6,22].

problems.title: A work-rate problem with two valid assignments
problems.question: Two workers together finish in 20 days. The first performs 1/18 of the job alone and the second then performs 1/9; these periods total 7 days. Find their solo times.
problems.idea: Use the solo times, so time for a fraction of the job is that fraction times the solo time.
formulas: If solo times are A,B, then 1/A+1/B=1/20 and A/18+B/9=7.
steps: The second equation gives A+2B=126, so A=126-2B.
The first gives AB=20(A+B). Substitute to get B²-73B+1260=0.
Thus (A,B)=(70,28) or (36,45). Both positive pairs satisfy the two original conditions.
problems.answer: First/second solo times: 70 and 28 days, or 36 and 45 days.
problems.note: The stated data allow both assignments; no additional comparison between worker speeds is supplied.

problems.title: Prove a two-variable inequality
problems.question: Prove $(x+5)(y+5)(x+y)\ge40xy$ for x,y>0, and give equality conditions.
problems.idea: Divide by xy and group three applications of AM-GM.
formulas: For positive u,v, u+v≥2√(uv), with equality iff u=v.
steps: After division, the left side is x+y+25/x+25/y+5(x/y+y/x+2).
We have x+25/x≥10 and y+25/y≥10. Also x/y+y/x≥2, making the last term at least 20.
Thus the divided expression is at least 10+10+20=40. Multiply by positive xy.
Equality requires x=5,y=5, which also makes x/y=y/x.
problems.answer: The inequality holds; equality exactly when x=y=5.

problems.title: Bound a sum of three square roots
problems.question: For positive a,b,c with a+b+c=4, prove $\sqrt{2a+1}+\sqrt{2b+1}+\sqrt{2c+1}\le\sqrt{33}$. State equality.
problems.idea: Apply Cauchy-Schwarz to the three radicals and three ones.
steps: The sum of squared radicals is (2a+1)+(2b+1)+(2c+1)=2·4+3=11.
Therefore their sum squared is at most 3·11=33.
Both sides are nonnegative, so taking square roots proves the bound.
Equality requires 2a+1=2b+1=2c+1, hence a=b=c=4/3.
problems.answer: At most √33, with equality at a=b=c=4/3.

problems.question: A triangle has sides 6,7,8. Find the ratio of the bisector to the median drawn from the vertex between sides 6 and 8.

problems.title: Inradius and circumradius of an isosceles triangle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has equal sides 60 and base 72. Find its inradius and circumradius.
problems.idea: Find its height, area and semiperimeter.
steps: The height is √(3600-1296)=48.
The area is 72·48/2=1728 and the semiperimeter is 96.
The inradius is 1728/96=18.
The circumradius is 60·60·72/(4·1728)=37.5.

problems.title: A trapezoid with a diameter base
problems.question: A trapezoid is inscribed in a circle of radius 9. Its large base is a diameter; its smaller base subtends a central angle β with sin(β/2)=1/9. Find the perimeter.
problems.idea: Use the chord formula and symmetry about the common perpendicular bisector of the bases.
formulas: Chord length=2R sin(β/2); circle equation and Pythagoras.
steps: The large base is 18 and the smaller is 2·9·(1/9)=2.
Place their endpoints at (-9,0),(9,0) and (-1,h),(1,h).
The circle gives h²=81-1=80. Each leg squared is (9-1)²+80=144, so each leg is 12.
The perimeter is 18+2+12+12=44.

problems.title: Maximum sum of the sines of acute right-triangle angles
problems.question: Find the greatest possible sum of the sines of the acute angles of a right triangle. When is it attained?
problems.idea: The two acute angles are complementary.
steps: The sum squared is at most 2(sin²α+cos²α)=2.
The sum is positive, so it is at most √2.
Equality requires sinα=cosα, hence α=45° and the other angle is 45°.
problems.answer: Maximum √2, attained in an isosceles right triangle.
